texts.preamble: Chittiprolu Srinivas Niranjan, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 9 July, 2024 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Surender Criminal Revision Case No.3 of 2010 Order:
texts.facts: 1. The revision petitioner/accused was convicted by the Court below for the offence under Section 16(1A) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short 'the Act') vide judgment in C.C.No.71 of 2007 dated 23.06.2008 by the learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Nalgonda. The case of the Food Inspector is that on 11.07.2006, he went to the shop of the petitioner M/s.Srinivasa Traders, of which the petitioner was the Proprietor. He purchased six sealed polythene packets containing Mustard seeds. The said seeds were kept for sale for human consumption. 3. The Inspector purchased six packets and made them into three packets by opening the sealed packets and sent them for analysis to FSL.
texts.arguments: 4. The only ground raised by the learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner is that under Rule 22 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, if the food is sold in packaged condition or in sealed container or package, they should be sent for analysis in its original condition without opening the package.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 4. The only ground raised by the learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner is that under Rule 22 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, if the food is sold in packaged condition or in sealed container or package, they should be sent for analysis in its original condition without opening the package.
